newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. envoy going home without deal - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy going home without deal - spokesman.

text.p: U.S. Middle East peace envoy Dennis Ross is leaving the region, having failed in a three-week mission to get Israel and the PLO to complete a deal on Hebron, a U.S. spokesman said on Sunday.
"I can confirm to you that Dennis Ross will leave tonight. He feels that the mediation role has been achieved, the assignment is complete," U.S. Embassy spokesman Richard Scorza told Reuters.

Ross, who is U.S. President Bill Clinton's special Middle East envoy, arrived on December 21 to try to get the sides to come to terms on a deal to give Palestinians self-rule in the West Bank town, a flashpoint of Arab-Israeli violence.

"The gap that remains is very small and it's really up to the parties now to come to an agreement but he (Ross) feels that his basic task right now is to brief the president and to get the president's advice on what the next steps are," the spokesman said.
Asked if Ross's mission was a failure, Scorza said: "It's up to the parties to make the deal."

The PLO said late on Saturday the talks were in crisis over a timetable for planned Israeli withdrawals from the West Bank following the Hebron pullback. Ross said on Saturday that the Hebron deal was basically complete but other hurdles remained.
